findings.chapter: Ch. 2 (What Actually Happens During Inference) — Table 2-2
findings.evidence: Table 2-2 row (PDF p.52): "Prefill: input tokens | 9,200 | 1,200 prompt + 8K context [canonical scenario][DERIVED]". Table 4-2 row (PDF p.103) labels the identical quantity: "Input tokens | 9,200 (1,200 prompt + 8,000 retrieved) | [canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION]", and Table 4-1's table-level provenance note (PDF p.90) states the convention: "an input or parameter assumption (traffic, latency target, price, token count) is [canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION]".
findings.issue: Provenance/epistemic-label inconsistency for a repeated load-bearing quantity: the canonical 9,200 input-token count is tagged [DERIVED] in Table 2-2 but [ASSUMPTION] in Tables 4-1/4-2, and the stated convention explicitly classifies token counts as assumptions. Under the book's own rule ("where this panel and that paragraph appear to differ, the stricter reading applies"), one of the two tags is wrong.
findings.fix_instruction: Re-tag the Table 2-2 row "Prefill: input tokens" as [canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION] (or, if the sum 1,200 + 8,000 is meant to be DERIVED, state that convention explicitly and align Table 4-2's row). While fixing, verify the adjacent Table 2-2 row "Model params | 70B | canonical scenario (Ch 4, Table 4-2)", which appears in the text layer without the [ASSUMPTION] epistemic tag that Table 3-1 ("[canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION] reference model") and Table 4-2 give the same quantity.
